land.text: al-Andalus, the Iberian rump of the Umayyad realm after the Abbasid revolution; Yusuf was governor from 747

predecessors.note: Cliopatria keeps the Umayyad Caliphate row to 756 and draws al-Andalus in its 751-756 shapes (473.6 and 445.1 thousand km2).

land.text: Córdoba and the south, taken by Abd al-Rahman in 756; the centre and north follow in 779-783

successors.note: The Emirate of Córdoba dossier books the whole 757 shape as a 757 gain; the Abd al-Rahman I page keeps the centre and north with Yusuf's supporters to 779.

capitals.name: Córdoba
capitals.note: Abd al-Rahman entered Córdoba after Musarah 'on the plains outside Córdoba'; Yusuf was then confined to the city by a truce.

capitals.name: Toledo
capitals.note: Yusuf 'fled to Toledo' (Abd al-Rahman page) and died there (759 in the infobox); Toledo is read as the supporters' centre. Approximate.

rulers.name: Yusuf ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Fihri
rulers.note: Governor of al-Andalus 747-750, then 'ruling unchallenged for nine years' as malik; defeated at Musarah in March 756, died at Toledo in 759.

correction.text: al-Andalus under Yusuf al-Fihri after the Umayyads fell in 750: the Cliopatria Umayyad Caliphate shape of 751-754

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria's Umayyad row still draws the old caliphate in 750 (5.2 M km2) and al-Andalus from 751 (473.6 thousand km2, bbox to 44.5 N, so it includes Septimania). The pages name no area; the shape stands as the extent of Yusuf's rule.

correction.text: the centre and north without Andalusia: 'most of central and northern al-Andalus (Toledo, Zaragoza, Barcelona)' which 'stayed with Yusuf's supporters until 779'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's Emirate of Córdoba shape of 757-762 (445.1 thousand km2) minus Andalusia is the reading; the page gives no boundary and says Zaragoza made a bid for autonomy in 756. Septimania fell to the Franks in 759 (Emirate dossier, not opened here).

ledger.note: 750: the Umayyads fall at Damascus and Yusuf al-Fihri keeps power in Spain. 'in Damascus the Umayyads were definitively overthrown in 750'; he then ruled as malik (king), not wali, 'ruling unchallenged for nine years'. Governor of al-Andalus since 747.

September 755: Abd al-Rahman lands at Almuñécar and takes Málaga and then Seville 'without violence' by early 756. The same year Yusuf crushed a revolt at Zaragoza (755) and a detachment sent against the Basques of Pamplona was annihilated (Yusuf page).

March 756: Yusuf is defeated at the battle of Musarah 'just outside Córdoba in March 756' (the Abd al-Rahman I page gives no date); Abd al-Rahman enters Córdoba and becomes 'the first independent Emir of Córdoba'.
14 May 756: Abd al-Rahman's reign begins (infobox) with Córdoba and the south; Yusuf fled to Toledo. The page gives no month for the entry into Córdoba, so the month is the reign's start.

region.text: the centre and north: Toledo, Zaragoza, Barcelona

ledger.note: 779: 'until 779 (submission of Zaragoza)' Yusuf's supporters held large parts of the north; Abd al-Rahman gave Zaragoza's governorship to al-Husayn ibn Yahya and took it by force in 783. The Emirate dossier books the whole land in 757, which the page does not support.

region.text: the supporters' remnant, ended by the submission of Zaragoza

ledger.note: 779: the last of the Fihrid party submits; local leaders (Sulayman al-Arabi) had met Charlemagne's envoys in 777-778 against Abd al-Rahman, which the Upper March lords (777-783) dossier should carry.

wars.name: Abd al-Rahman I's conquest of al-Andalus
wars.outcome: Abd al-Rahman landed at Almuñécar in September 755, took Seville by March 756 and beat Yusuf at Musarah in March 756; the north and centre resisted until 779-783.
wars.note: The page gives no date for the Musarah battle or for Yusuf's death in Toledo; the Yusuf page has 759.

certainty.note: Al-Andalus before 756 is drawn from Cliopatria's shape; the supporters' territory after 756 is a reading of the pages' towns.

sources.title: Yusuf ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Fihri
sources.note: Governor 747-750, malik 750-756, Zaragoza revolt 755, Musarah March 756, death 759 at Toledo.

sources.title: Abd al-Rahman I
sources.note: Landing at Almuñécar Sept 755, Seville by March 756, reign from 14 May 756, Yusuf's supporters hold the centre and north to 779, Zaragoza 779 and 783.

notes: Written for eu-12-x (named as a counterpart by the Umayyad and Emirate of Córdoba dossiers under the string 'Fihrid governors of al-Andalus' and by eu-12-a); two pages. Cliopatria has no row. The Umayyad Caliphate dossier books the 750 loss and the Emirate of Córdoba dossier the 756 founding and the 757 gain with this string as counterpart; the 757 gain should be split (south 756, centre and north 779-783) in line with the Abd al-Rahman I page. Disagreements: Musarah in March 756 (Yusuf page) against an undated battle and a reign from 14 May 756 (Abd al-Rahman I page); Yusuf's death 759 (infobox) against 'two or three years' of survival at Toledo. Not settled: Septimania (Narbonne, Roussillon) was part of Cliopatria's 751 shape and the Franks took it in 759-760 per the Emirate dossier, which the pages opened here do not mention; the rebellious lords of the Upper March 777-783 (Sulayman al-Arabi) need a dossier if wanted (eu-12-a suggested rebellious-lords-of-the-upper-march); the 740s Berber revolt and the pre-750 governorship are not covered. The note on Córdoba as capital is a reading.
